events.title: First Earth Day Celebrated
events.description: An estimated 20 million Americans took part in rallies, teach-ins, and demonstrations across the United States to demand environmental protection. The event was organized by Senator Gaylord Nelson and activist Denis Hayes.
events.significance: Earth Day is widely credited with launching the modern environmental movement and led to the creation of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and landmark laws such as the Clean Air Act. It is now observed globally by more than a billion people each year.

events.title: Pedro Álvares Cabral Reaches Brazil
events.description: Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral, leading a fleet bound for India, sighted land on the coast of present-day Bahia and claimed it for Portugal.
events.significance: Cabral's landing began Portuguese colonization of Brazil, shaping the language, culture, and history of the largest country in South America.

events.title: U.S. Congress Mandates 'In God We Trust' on Coins
events.description: The Coinage Act of 1864 authorized the two-cent piece and allowed the motto 'In God We Trust' to appear on U.S. coinage for the first time, during the Civil War.
events.significance: The motto later spread to other denominations and was made the official national motto of the United States in 1956.

events.title: Death of Richard Nixon
events.description: Richard Nixon, the 37th President of the United States, died at age 81 in New York City after suffering a stroke four days earlier.
events.significance: Nixon was the only U.S. president to resign from office, following the Watergate scandal. His legacy also includes opening relations with China and easing Cold War tensions with the Soviet Union.

events.title: Birth of Immanuel Kant
events.description: The philosopher Immanuel Kant was born in Königsberg, Prussia, where he would spend nearly his entire life as a scholar and professor.
events.significance: Kant's works, especially the Critique of Pure Reason, transformed metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics, and remain foundational to modern Western philosophy.
